Benchmark Screening Methods: Classification Accuracy

Source: R/61-BenchAcc.R
BenchAcc.Rd

Computes binary classification metrics for every screening method present in the input, by comparing each method's per-cell labels against ground-truth labels. "Positive" is treated as the positive class and all other labels as negative, so the accuracy of different screening methods can be compared on the same cells.

Usage

BenchAcc(obj, ...)

# S3 method for class 'Seurat'
BenchAcc(
  obj,
  bench_config = character(),
  ...,
  verbose = getFuncOption("verbose"),
  nthreads = getFuncOption("nthreads")
)

# S3 method for class '`SigBridgeR::BenchAccConfig`'
BenchAcc(obj, ..., verbose = getFuncOption("verbose"))

# S3 method for class '`SigBridgeR::ScreenMethodResult`'
BenchAcc(obj, ...)

# Default S3 method
BenchAcc(obj, ...)

Arguments

obj

The object to evaluate, one of:

  • a Seurat object whose meta.data contains screening method results (columns named after screening methods, e.g. "Scissor");

  • a ScreenMethodResult object, whose scRNA_data slot is evaluated;

  • a BenchAccConfig object, whose screen_method entries are all run through Screen() first and the accumulated labels are evaluated in a single pass.

...

Additional arguments passed between the S3 methods. Currently unused apart from forwarding

bench_config

character. Ground-truth labels used as the reference: either a length-one column name in obj@meta.data, or a per-cell label vector of length ncol(obj). Must contain a "Positive" label. For a BenchAccConfig input the labels are taken from the same-named slot.

verbose

Logical. Whether to report progress information. Default: TRUE.

nthreads

Integer. Number of threads used by the C++ metric computation. Default: 2L.

Value

A named list with one element per screening method found in meta.data. Each element is a 1-row numeric matrix with columns TPR, FPR, TNR, FNR, F1, Accuracy and so on.

Details

Dispatch

BenchAcc() dispatches on the class of obj: a BenchAccConfig is screened first, a ScreenMethodResult is unwrapped to its scRNA_data slot, and BenchAcc.Seurat() performs the computation. Unsupported classes abort with an informative error.

Method detection

Columns of obj@meta.data whose names match a supported screening method (case-insensitive) are taken as the predicted labels; other columns are ignored. The function aborts when no such column exists.

Ground truth

A length-one bench_config is looked up as a column of obj@meta.data; otherwise it is used directly as a per-cell label vector. The labels must include "Positive", and the vector form must have one element per cell.

Metrics

With P, N, TP, FP, TN and FN denoting the numbers of positive cells, negative cells, true/false positives and true/false negatives

See also

BenchAccConfig(), ScreenMethodResult, Screen(), BenchGSEA(), BenchMemory(), BenchGeneScore()

Other Benchmark: BenchGSEA(), BenchGeneScore(), BenchMemory()

Examples

counts <- matrix(
  rep(1:10, 6L),
  nrow = 10L,
  dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:10), paste0("Cell", 1:6))
)
obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts)
#> Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix.
obj$truth <- c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Positive", "Negative")
obj$Scissor <- c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative")
BenchAcc(obj, bench_config = "truth", verbose = FALSE)
#> $`c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative")`
#>                                                                              TPR
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative") 0.6666667
#>                                                                        FPR TNR
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative")   0   1
#>                                                                              FNR
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative") 0.3333333
#>                                                                         F1
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative") 0.8
#>                                                                         Accuracy
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative") 0.8333333
#>                                                                        Precision
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative")         1
#>                                                                           Recall
#> c("Positive", "Negative", "Positive", "Other", "Negative", "Negative") 0.6666667
#>
